verses.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Go to Pharaoh and tell him, 'This is what the LORD says: Let my people go, so that they can worship me.
If you refuse to let them go, I will send a plague of frogs on your whole country.

The Nile will be full of frogs. They will come up into your palace, into your bedroom, and onto your bed. They will go into the houses of your officials and onto your people, and into your ovens and the bowls where you make bread.
The frogs will jump on you, on your people, and on all your officials.'"
Then the LORD said to Moses, "Tell Aaron, 'Stretch out your hand with your staff over the rivers, the streams, and the pools, and make frogs come up onto the land of Egypt.'"
So Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt, and the frogs came up and covered the land.
But the magicians did the same thing with their secret arts. They also made frogs come up onto the land of Egypt.
Then Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron and said, "Pray to the LORD to take the frogs away from me and my people. Then I will let the people go to offer sacrifices to the LORD."
Moses said to Pharaoh, "You may choose the time. When should I pray for you, your officials, and your people, so that the frogs leave you and your houses, and stay only in the Nile?"
"Tomorrow," Pharaoh said. Moses replied, "It will be as you say, so that you will know that there is no one like the LORD our God.
The frogs will leave you, your houses, your officials, and your people. They will stay only in the Nile."
Moses and Aaron left Pharaoh, and Moses cried out to the LORD about the frogs he had brought on Pharaoh.
And the LORD did what Moses asked. The frogs died in the houses, in the yards, and in the fields.
The people piled them up in heaps, and the whole land stank.
But when Pharaoh saw that the trouble was over, he made his heart stubborn and would not listen to Moses and Aaron, just as the LORD had said.
Then the LORD said to Moses, "Tell Aaron, 'Stretch out your staff and strike the dust of the ground, and the dust will turn into lice all over the land of Egypt.'"
They did this. Aaron stretched out his hand with the staff and struck the dust of the ground, and lice came on people and animals. All the dust in the whole land of Egypt turned into lice.
The magicians tried to make lice with their secret arts, but they could not. And the lice stayed on people and animals.
The magicians said to Pharaoh, "This is the finger of God!" But Pharaoh's heart was stubborn, and he would not listen, just as the LORD had said.

Then the LORD said to Moses, "Get up early in the morning and stand in front of Pharaoh when he goes out to the water. Say to him, 'This is what the LORD says: Let my people go, so that they can worship me.

If you do not let my people go, I will send swarms of flies on you, your officials, your people, and into your houses. The houses of the Egyptians will be full of flies, and so will the ground they stand on.
But on that day I will treat the land of Goshen differently, where my people live. There will be no swarms of flies there. Then you will know that I, the LORD, am in this land.
I will make a difference between my people and your people. This sign will happen tomorrow.'"
And the LORD did this. Thick swarms of flies poured into Pharaoh's palace and into the houses of his officials. All over Egypt the land was ruined by the flies.
Then Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron and said, "Go, offer sacrifices to your God here in this land."

But Moses said, "That would not be right. The sacrifices we offer to the LORD our God would be disgusting to the Egyptians. If we offer sacrifices that are disgusting to them right in front of their eyes, will they not throw stones at us?
We must take a three-day journey into the desert and offer sacrifices to the LORD our God, as he commands us."
Pharaoh said, "I will let you go to offer sacrifices to the LORD your God in the desert, but you must not go very far. Now pray for me."

Moses answered, "As soon as I leave you, I will pray to the LORD. Tomorrow the flies will leave Pharaoh, his officials, and his people. But Pharaoh must not trick us again by refusing to let the people go to offer sacrifices to the LORD."
Then Moses left Pharaoh and prayed to the LORD.
And the LORD did what Moses asked. The flies left Pharaoh, his officials, and his people. Not one fly was left.
But this time also Pharaoh made his heart stubborn and would not let the people go.
